title: Teleported free energy simulations
abstract: Escorted free energy simulations reduce dissipation with a flow field that follows the equilibrium distribution. A continuous flow, however, cannot transfer probability between metastable basins. We show that any escort then faces a variance floor set by the change in basin weights, and lift it by adding teleportation: jumps at a rate proportional to the driving rate. We derive the corresponding nonequilibrium identity, the zero-dissipation condition, and the minimal number of jumps it requires, and illustrate the gain on an exactly solvable model and a tilted double well.
summary: This paper introduces 'teleported free energy simulations' to overcome limitations in calculating free energy differences in systems with separated metastable states. By augmenting continuous flow dynamics with controlled probability jumps (teleportation), the method eliminates the variance floor found in standard escort simulations. This provides a highly accurate and theoretically justified tool for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating free energy differences ($\Delta F$) between two equilibrium states using non-equilibrium simulation methods, especially when the system involves metastable basins separated by high barriers.
main_result: The introduction of 'teleportation' (jumps) to the standard 'escorted' flow field successfully removes the variance floor inherent in continuous flow methods, allowing for accurate $\Delta F$ estimation even when probability must move between basins.
method: The authors combine continuous flow dynamics (escorting) with discrete jump processes (teleportation) to modify the underlying master equation governing the phase-space density evolution.
model_or_system: The analysis uses a general Hamiltonian $H(z, \lambda)$ describing a system with metastable basins. Specific examples include a two-basin model and the tilted double well potential, where the parameter $\lambda$ drives the system between states.
key_observables: Free energy difference ($\Delta F$), dissipated work ($\langle W angle - \Delta F$), variance of the work estimator, and the mean number of inter-basin jumps ($\langle n angle$).
important_parameters: The simulation time $	au$, the temperature parameter $ eta$, and the relative weights/populations of the metastable basins ($\pi_A, \pi_B$).
main_assumptions: The standard escort method fails when the driving parameter $\lambda$ changes the relative populations of metastable states; the method assumes that the required jump activity is governed by the total variation distance between basin populations.
figures_summary: Figures compare free energy estimates using plain, escorted, and teleported dynamics, demonstrating that teleportation significantly reduces the variance floor, especially in the double well potential.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the non-equilibrium work relation and the failure of continuous escorting when basin populations change. It then introduces teleportation to lift the variance floor, deriving the zero-dissipation condition and the minimal required jump rate. Finally, it illustrates these concepts using solvable models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, theoretically grounded extension to advanced sampling techniques, offering a robust way to calculate free energy differences in complex, multi-basin systems where standard methods fail due to rare events.

Figure 2(a) shows the estimates for h = 2, with N = 107 trajectories per point for all three methods. About a hundred of them, NπR(0) ≃130, start in the right well, so the rare events that matter are sampled and all estimates are correct on average. The difference lies in the fluctuations. Without teleports the error bars are about 0.04 and do not shrink with τ: the measured relative variance of e−βW is 2 × 104 at every switching time, with and without the escort, right on the floor of Eq. (14). Slower switching does not help, because the barrier is never crossed, and no escort can help either.
